inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age: In the pre-k room infants and prek children were observed to be mixed, the age of the youngest child was 15 months and the oldest was 4 years old. There was more than 18 months between the youngest and oldest child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: Two caregivers in the nap room were unaware of the ages of children in their group. When asked they stated the youngest was almost 2yrs but not two yet. When asked the child's age in months. They stated they did not know. When asked about the age of the oldest. Both pointed to the same child. One said the child was 5yrs old and the other said the child was either 8yr or 9yrs.     NOTE: The ages of children present were 2yrs to 8yrs old. The caregivers did not have information avialable to show the ages of each child in care. One caregiver stated the paperwork available was not updated.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the inspection, a child was observed standing in the hall and refusing to go in the nap room. After unsuccussful attempts to get the child into the classroom, the caregiver left the child in the hall with no further interaction. The child could not be seen by either caregiver and stayed in the hall for approximately 20 minutes. The director was observed to make attempts to placed the child in the room but was unsuccessful as well. There were multiple time were the child was left unsupervised including one time where the director walked past the child to go to the kitcen     Another child was observed running out of the room before the caregiver got up to return the child to the room. While speaking with the director, a child left the room unspervised and was found in the hall by the director. The child stated they wanted water. The director explained they could not leave without permission and returned the child to the group.      One child was observed lying down and trying to sleep on a table. Two children were running around and ran into each other and fell on top of another child. Neither caregiver present intervened in any of these observations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device: During the inspection, the pre-k caregiver was heard telling a child one two occasions they would not go outside becuase of their behavior. The caregiver stated that for discipline children sit  for 10 minutes and if the whole group is misbehaving all children aare required to have a 10 minute quite time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2805(10))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: The caregiver in care of 10 children 2-4yrs old was not aware the ages of children in their care. The caregiver informed CCR that the posted list of children was not updated
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the inspection, the caregiver was observed to step out of the classroom while children were still inside. CHildren were seen phyically fighting and climbing on top of each other. Two children were seen crawling and walking on furniture.     While on the playground, children continued to walk inside the buliding without a caregiver. At one poinit, 4 children walked into the building without the caregiver being aware of it before another caregiver inside escorted the children back outside.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions: A caregiver with a provisional background check with conditions stating they may never be alone with children was observed to be left unspervised multiple times during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions (26 TAC §745.635(3))

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: Multiple children were observed sleeping on unlabeled napmats. According to the caregiver, the children pulled them off but they had not yet been replaced.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: A caregiver was observed to be on their personal cell phone during naptime supervsion. CCR stood infront of the caregiver for approximately 30 seconds before the caregiver was aware of CCR's presence in the classroom. Another caregiver present called their name multiple times before the caregiver looked up and acknowledged CCR's presence.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age: A child was observed sleeping on the bare floor. Another child was not observed to have a cot/mat for naptime. According to staff there were not enough for all children. Cots/mats are not kept for drop-in children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age (26 TAC §746.4503(a))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: A bottle of chemical cleaner and bleach water spray bottle in the pre-k room and Clorox wipes in the bathroom used by children were observed to in unlocked cabinets in reach of children
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: Infant feeding instruction was not updated for two infants. Last update for one was 5/28/25 and the other last update for the second infant was 5/5/2025.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: There was no emergency contact information for one out of four records checked.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: Current first aid and Cpr was not observed on file for the director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Release Information: There was no release information on file for one out of four files checked.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Release Information (26 TAC §746.605(7))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: Health statement was missing on one out of four files checked.
Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Must Use for Each Child in When Transporting and be Properly Installed: Two sealt belt in one of the vans used for transportation needed to be fixed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Must Use for Each Child in When Transporting and be Properly Installed (26 TAC §746.5607(a))
